sentences.text:
The present petition has been filed seeking quashing of FIR No. 1121/2021 dated 28th December,
2021, under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC) registered at Police Station Samaypur Badli on the ground of settlement.
2. The petitioner no.1 is the husband of the respondent no.2 and the petitioners no.2 to 4 are family members of the petitioner no.1.
The marriage of the petitioner no.1 and the respondent no.2 was solemnized on 3rd March, 2019, according to Hindu rites and ceremonies.
3. Disputes arose between the parties and their respective families, This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 19/09/2023 at 23:05:30 which resulted in filing of the FIR by the respondent no.2 against the petitioners.

4. Subsequently, the parties have settled their disputes in terms of Settlement Agreement dated 25th Rahul Mishra & Ors vs The State Of Nct Of Delhi & Anr on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141624989/
1 July, 2023, entered into between the parties before the Delhi Mediation Centre, Rohini District Courts, which has been filed with the petition.
5. Issue notice.

sentences.text:
6. Notice is accepted by the learned APP appearing on behalf of the State and by the counsel appearing on behalf of the respondent no. 2.
7.
The respondent no.2 is present in Court and has been identified by her counsel and by the Investigating Officer (IO).
She informs the Court that she has settled the matter of her own free will and without any coercion.
She further states that she has no objection to quashing of the FIR.
8. The petitioners are also present in Court and have been identified by their counsel.
They affirm the statement of the respondent no.2 and undertake to abide by the terms of settlement arrived at between the parties.
9. In terms of the Settlement, parties are to withdraw all cases filed by them and shall reside together as husband and wife.

10. Considering the above settlement between the parties and the chances of conviction of the petitioners being remote and bleak, there is no use continuing with proceedings of the present FIR as it would be a misuse of the process of the Court and an unnecessary burden on the State exchequer.
Hence, it would be in the interest of justice to quash the aforementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
There is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.
11. Consequently, FIR No.1121/2021 at Police Station Samaypur Badli This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 19/09/2023 at 23:05:30 and proceedings pursuant thereto are quashed.
12. The petition stands disposed of.

AMIT BANSAL, J.
